content: I'll read the test image to analyze the plant disease symptoms.

**Visual Analysis:**

- **Affected part:** Banana fruit (fingers/tips)
- **Key visual features:**
  - Green banana fingers with dark brown/black lesions at the tips and on the fruit surface
  - The lesions appear sunken, dark, and necrotic — concentrated at the distal (tip) ends of the fingers
  - The image is labeled "Wound anthracnose"
  - Text mentions symptoms observed when fruits are unpacked after sea transport

**Reasoning:**
- The dark, necrotic lesions on the banana fruit surface/tips are characteristic of **Anthracnose** caused by *Colletotrichum musae*
- Cigar End Rot also affects the tip of banana fingers, but it tends to cause a dry, shriveled, cigar-shaped rotting specifically at the blossom end — not the scattered dark spots seen here
- The image explicitly labels this as "Wound anthracnose," and the lesion pattern (dark, sunken spots on green banana skin) matches Anthracnose perfectly
- This is distinct from leaf diseases (Cordana Leaf Spot, Yellow and Black Sigatoka), systemic diseases (Panama Disease), or viruses (Bunchy Top)
